sections.overview: This small Central American cichlid inhabits Atlantic-slope rivers from Belize to Nicaragua.
sections.identification: It is known for bright blue eyes; males generally grow larger than females.
sections.habitat: Adults occupy shallow lake margins and slower river reaches over sand, mud or rock.
sections.diet: Field accounts describe benthic omnivory, including small invertebrates and algae gathered from the bottom.
sections.behavior: Pairs defend a territory during spawning and parental care, consistent with other cave-breeding Cryptoheros cichlids.
sections.reproduction: It lays eggs on a substrate and the two parents tend the brood; laboratory work documents rapid early development.
sections.ecology: The accepted name is Cryptoheros spilurus, although older literature also uses Archocentrus and Cichlasoma.
sections.conservation: A current global assessment is listed as Data Deficient, so this should not be read as evidence of low risk.
